questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the natural source of salicylic acid?
questions.solution:
Salicylic acid occurs naturally in willow plants, derived from salicin compounds present in willow bark. This botanical source has been historically recognized for its analgesic and anti-inflammatory properties, attributed to the metabolic conversion of salicin to salicylic acid.

Alternative options represent distinct phytochemical sources: cinnamon contains cinnamaldehyde, turmeric contains curcuminoids, and Indian gooseberry is rich in ascorbic acid, none of which relate to salicylic acid biosynthesis.

The correct identification is willow plant.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following compounds has lowest boiling point?
questions.solution:
The boiling point of alcohols is influenced by hydrogen bonding and London dispersion forces, both present in these compounds.

Hydrogen bonding occurs through the hydroxyl group, contributing significantly to boiling points. London dispersion forces increase with molecular size and surface area, strengthening with additional carbon atoms.

Methanol ($\mathrm{CH_3 OH}$) possesses only one carbon atom, resulting in the weakest London dispersion forces among the alcohols. While hydrogen bonding is present, the reduced molecular size leads to lower overall intermolecular attraction.

$\text{Less energy is required to overcome these weaker forces, resulting in methanol's lower boiling point.}$

The correct answer is D.

questions.q:
Identify the product ' $A$ ' in the following reaction,
Anisole $\xrightarrow[398 \mathrm{~K}]{\mathrm{HI}} \mathrm{A}+$ Iodomethane
questions.solution:
The cleavage of anisole with hydroiodic acid at 398 K proceeds through nucleophilic substitution on the alkyl carbon of this aryl alkyl ether system.

The aryl-oxygen bond possesses partial double bond character due to resonance stabilization, rendering it resistant to cleavage. In contrast, the alkyl-oxygen bond is more labile. Protonation of the ether oxygen by HI yields an oxonium ion intermediate, which is then subject to $S_N2$ attack by the iodide nucleophile.

This nucleophilic attack occurs exclusively at the methyl carbon, as the phenyl group offers both steric hindrance and electronic stabilization that disfavors cleavage at that position. The reaction therefore produces phenol and iodomethane.

Thus, product A is benzenol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the product formed when Hex-3-enenitrile is reduced with diisobutylaluminium hydride followed by acid hydrolysis?
questions.solution:
Structure identification: Hex-3-ennenitrile corresponds to $\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-CH=CH-CH_2-CN}$. Reduction with DIBAL-H selectively reduces the nitrile to an imine without affecting the isolated alkene: $\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-CH=CH-CH_2-CN \xrightarrow{DIBAL-H} CH_3-CH_2-CH=CH-CH_2-CH=NH}$. Acid hydrolysis converts the imine to the aldehyde: $\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-CH=CH-CH_2-CH=NH \xrightarrow{H_3 O^+} CH_3-CH_2-CH=CH-CH_2-CHO + NH_3}$. The product $\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-CH=CH-CH_2-CHO}$ is hex-3-enal. Option comparison:
A: Hexanal ($\mathrm{CH_3(CH_2)_4CHO}$, saturated)
B: Hexan-3-one ($\mathrm{CH_3CH_2COCH_2CH_2CH_3}$, ketone)
C: Hex-3-enal (matches product)
D: Hexanoic acid ($\mathrm{CH_3(CH_2)_4COOH}$, carboxylic acid)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify tertiary amine from following.
questions.solution:
Tertiary amines are characterized by a nitrogen atom bonded to three alkyl or aryl groups, with no hydrogen substituents.

Cyclohexanamine ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_{11}\text{NH}_2$) contains nitrogen bonded to one cyclohexyl group and two hydrogen atoms, making it a primary amine.

Ethane 1,2-diamine ($\text{H}_2\text{N}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{NH}_2$) contains two nitrogen atoms, each bonded to an alkyl fragment and two hydrogens, classifying it as a primary diamine.

N-Phenylbenzeneamine ($(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5)_2\text{NH}$) contains nitrogen bonded to two phenyl groups and one hydrogen, designating it as a secondary amine.

N-Ethyl-N-Methylpropan-2-amine ($(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH}-\text{N}(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5)(\text{CH}_3)$) contains nitrogen bonded to an isopropyl group, an ethyl group, and a methyl group. With three alkyl substituents and no hydrogen atoms, this is a tertiary amine.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify least stable species from following.
questions.solution:
Electron-donating groups stabilize positively charged species through the +I effect, with alkyl groups providing increasing stabilization as their number increases.

$\mathrm{NH_4^+}$ lacks alkyl substituents and receives no inductive stabilization from electron-donating groups.

$\mathrm{R-NH_3+}$ gains modest stabilization from one alkyl group, while $\mathrm{R_2NH_2^+}$ benefits more strongly from two alkyl groups. $\mathrm{R_3NH^+}$ achieves maximum stability through three electron-donating alkyl groups.

The stability order follows the number of alkyl substituents: $\mathrm{R_3NH^+ \gt R_2NH_2+ \gt RNH_3+ \gt NH_4^+}$.

The least stable species is therefore $\mathrm{NH4^+}$, corresponding to option A.

questions.q: Identify the carbon atom numbered from $\mathrm{C}_1{ }^{\prime}$ to $\mathrm{C}_5{ }^{\prime}$ of monosaccharide unit of DNA nucleotide that lacks oxygen atom from -OH group.
questions.solution:
The monosaccharide unit in DNA is deoxyribose, a pentose sugar distinguished from ribose by the absence of oxygen at the C-2′ position.
Ribose contains a hydroxyl group (-OH) at C-2′, whereas deoxyribose substitutes this with a hydrogen atom (-H).
All other carbon atoms (C-1′, C-3′, C-4′, C-5′) either include oxygen in hydroxyl groups, the furanose ring, or participate in glycosidic or phosphodiester bonds.

$\boxed{B}$

questions.q: Identify acidic amino acid from following list represented by three letter symbols.
questions.solution:
Amino acids are classified based on their side chain properties as neutral (polar or non-polar), acidic, or basic. Among the given options:

Threonine has a polar hydroxyl group, making it neutral polar. Tryptophan's indole ring classifies it as neutral non-polar. Histidine contains an imidazole group that can accept protons, classifying it as basic.

Glutamic acid possesses an additional carboxyl group in its side chain that donates protons, making it acidic.

Acetic acid $\xrightarrow[\Delta]{\text { Thionyl chloride }} \mathrm{A} \xrightarrow{\text { Ammonia }} \mathrm{B}$
questions.solution:
Acetic acid undergoes reaction with thionyl chloride to form acetyl chloride:
$\mathrm{CH_3COOH + SOCl_2 \xrightarrow{\Delta} CH_3COCl + SO_2 \uparrow + HCl \uparrow}$

Acetyl chloride then reacts with ammonia via nucleophilic acyl substitution to form acetamide:
$\mathrm{CH_3COCl + 2NH_3 \rightarrow CH_3CONH_2 + NH_4Cl}$

The sequence produces acetamide, which corresponds to option D.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{D}}$

questions.q:
Identify the product formed in the following reaction.
$\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{Mg} \mathrm{Br} \xrightarrow[\text { ii) dil. } \mathrm{HCl}]{\text { i) Dry ice/ dry ether }} \text { Product }$
questions.solution:
Grignard Reaction with Carbon Dioxide

Ethylmagnesium bromide ($\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{MgBr}$) reacts as a nucleophile with carbon dioxide ($\mathrm{CO}_2$) in dry ether, attacking the electrophilic carbon to form a magnesium carboxylate salt.

$\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{MgBr} + \mathrm{CO}_2 \rightarrow \mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{COO}^{-}\mathrm{Mg}^{+}\mathrm{Br}$

Hydrolysis with dilute hydrochloric acid liberates the carboxylic acid.

$\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{COO}^{-}\mathrm{Mg}^{+}\mathrm{Br} + \mathrm{HCl} \rightarrow \mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{COOH} + \mathrm{MgBrCl}$

The product is propanoic acid ($\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{COOH}$), corresponding to option B.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is correct decreasing order of bond length regarding $\mathrm{N}_2, \mathrm{O}_2$ and $\mathrm{Cl}_2$ ?
questions.solution:
Bond lengths decrease with increasing bond multiplicity and increase with larger atomic radii. The bond order and atomic size determine the bond length: $\mathrm{N}_2$ has a triple bond, $\mathrm{O}_2$ a double bond, and $\mathrm{Cl}_2$ a single bond.

$\mathrm{N}_2$: $\mathrm{N} \equiv \mathrm{N}$, bond length $\approx$ 109.8 pm
$\mathrm{O}_2$: $\mathrm{O} = \mathrm{O}$, bond length $\approx$ 121 pm
$\mathrm{Cl}_2$: $\mathrm{Cl} - \mathrm{Cl}$, bond length $\approx$ 199 pm

Since higher bond order corresponds to shorter bonds, and chlorine has the largest atomic radius, the order is $\mathrm{Cl}_2 \gt \mathrm{O}_2 \gt \mathrm{N}_2$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The attractive interactions between cations and mobile electrons in metallic solid is called
questions.solution:
olids, metal atoms lose valence electrons to form cations, while delocalized electrons form a shared "sea" throughout the structure.

The electrostatic attraction between these positive metal ions and negative delocalized electrons constitutes the metallic bond, often described as the electron sea model.


Other bond types differ significantly: ionic bonding involves complete electron transfer between atoms, covalent bonding involves electron sharing between specific atoms, and weak dipole-dipole interactions occur between polar molecules rather than within metallic structures.


The correct classification is therefore $\boxed{\text{D}}$.

Average Rate of Reaction

The average rate is defined as $\frac{\Delta[\text{Product}]}{\Delta t}$ for a product's concentration change over time.

Given $\Delta[\text{Product}] = 0.05\ \text{M}$ and $\Delta t = 20\ \text{s}$, we compute:

$\text{Average Rate} = \frac{0.05}{20} = 0.0025\ \text{M s}^{-1}$.

This matches option A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The slope of a graph $\log [A]_t$ versus ' $t$ ' for first order reaction is $-2.5 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~s}^{-1}$. Find rate constant of the reaction?
questions.solution:
The integrated rate law for a first-order reaction is expressed as $\ln[A]_t = -kt + \ln[A]_0$.

Converting to base-10 logarithms using the identity $\ln x = 2.303 \log x$ yields:

$\log[A]_t = -\frac{k}{2.303}t + \log[A]_0$

This represents a linear relationship where the slope is $-\frac{k}{2.303}$.

Given the measured slope of the plot of $\log[A]_t$ versus time is $-2.5 \times 10^{-3}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$, we equate:

$-\frac{k}{2.303} = -2.5 \times 10^{-3}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$

Solving for the rate constant $k$:

$k = 2.303 \times 2.5 \times 10^{-3}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1} = 5.7575 \times 10^{-3}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$

Rounded to three significant figures, $k \approx 5.76 \times 10^{-3}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$, confirming that option C is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is reduction potential of hydrogen gas electrode when pure hydrogen gas is at 1 atmospheric pressure and platinum electrode is in contact with HCl solution of PH 1 at 298 K ?
questions.solution:
The reduction potential for the hydrogen electrode under specified conditions is determined using the Nernst equation:

$E_{red} = E^0_{red} - \frac{0.0592}{n} \log \frac{P_{H_2}}{[H^+]^2}$

Substituting $E^0_{red} = 0 \text{ V}$, $P_{H_2} = 1 \text{ atm}$, and $n = 2$, with $[H^+] = 10^{-\text{pH}} = 10^{-1} \text{ M}$, yields:

$E_{red} = - \frac{0.0592}{2} \log \frac{1}{(10^{-1})^2} = - \frac{0.0592}{2} \log(10^2)$

Simplifying the logarithmic term, $\log(10^2) = 2$, results in:

$E_{red} = -0.0592 \text{ V}$

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{B}}$

questions.q:
Which of the following net cell reaction takes place in a galvanic cell containing copper electrode and standard hydrogen electrode ?
$\mathrm{E}^{\circ}\left(\mathrm{Cu}_{(\mathrm{aq})}^{+2} \mid \mathrm{Cu}_{(\mathrm{s})}\right)=+0 \cdot 34 \mathrm{~V}$
questions.solution:
Net Cell Reaction Determination via Standard Potentials

A cell's net reaction is governed by standard reduction potentials: the higher potential species undergoes reduction (cathode), while the lower is oxidized (anode). Given $E^{\circ}_{\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}|\mathrm{Cu}} = +0.34\ \mathrm{V}$ and $E^{\circ}_{2\mathrm{H}^+|\mathrm{H}_2} = 0.00\ \mathrm{V}$, copper ions reduce and hydrogen oxidizes.

Cathode reaction: $\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}_{(\mathrm{aq})} + 2\mathrm{e}^- \longrightarrow \mathrm{Cu}_{(\mathrm{s})}$
Anode reaction: $\mathrm{H}_{2(\mathrm{g})} \longrightarrow 2\mathrm{H}^+_{(\mathrm{aq})} + 2\mathrm{e}^-$

Net cell reaction: $\mathrm{H}_{2(\mathrm{g})} + \mathrm{Cu}^{2+}_{(\mathrm{aq})} \longrightarrow 2\mathrm{H}^+_{(\mathrm{aq})} + \mathrm{Cu}_{(\mathrm{s})}$

This yields $E^{\circ}_{\mathrm{cell}} = 0.34\ \mathrm{V} - 0.00\ \mathrm{V} = +0.34\ \mathrm{V}$, confirming spontaneity. Among the options, only B matches this reaction.

Final answer: B

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a fittig reaction?
questions.solution:
The Fittig reaction couples two aryl halides with sodium in dry ether to form a biaryl compound:

$2 \text{Ar-X} + 2\text{Na} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} \text{Ar-Ar} + 2\text{NaX}$

Option A: $\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{Br}+\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{Br}+2 \mathrm{Na} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} \mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5-\mathrm{CH}_3+2 \mathrm{NaBr}$ involves an aryl halide and an alkyl halide, characteristic of the Wurtz–Fittig reaction.

Option B: $2 \mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{Br}+2 \mathrm{Na} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} \mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{H}_5-\mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{H}_5+2 \mathrm{NaBr}$ uses only alkyl halides, indicating the Wurtz reaction.

Option C: $2 \mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{Br}+2 \mathrm{Na} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} \mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}_3+2 \mathrm{NaBr}$ also uses alkyl halides and is another Wurtz reaction.

Option D: $2 \mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{Br}+2 \mathrm{Na} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} \mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5-\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5+2 \mathrm{NaBr}$ couples two aryl halides to form biphenyl, matching the definition of the Fittig reaction.

The Fittig reaction is represented by option D.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the product obtained when alkene is reacted with cold and dilute alkaline potassium permanganate?
questions.solution:
Baeyer's test employs cold, dilute alkaline potassium permanganate as a mild oxidizing agent to achieve syn-dihydroxylation. The alkene undergoes addition of two hydroxyl groups across the double bond from the same face, forming a vicinal diol (glycol).

The general reaction is $\text{R-CH=CH-R'} + \text{KMnO}_4 \text{ (cold, dilute, alkaline)} \rightarrow \text{R-CH(OH)-CH(OH)-R'}$.

Option A (alkanol) is incorrect as it specifies a single hydroxyl group. Option C (glycerol) is a triol and does not result from this reaction. Option D (alkanoic acid) forms under stronger oxidative cleavage conditions. The product is specifically a glycol, making option B correct.

Identify 'A' in the following reaction.
$\mathrm{A}+\text { chloromethane } \xrightarrow[\mathrm{AlCl}_3]{\text { Anhydrous }} 1 \text {-chlorotoluene }+4 \text {-chlorotoluene }$
questions.solution:
The Friedel-Crafts alkylation reaction proceeds with chloromethane and anhydrous $\mathrm{AlCl_3}$ catalyst to yield 1-chlorotoluene and 4-chlorotoluene isomers.

In this electrophilic substitution, the methyl carbocation $\mathrm{CH_3^+}$ attacks the aromatic ring.
For benzene, methylation produces toluene rather than chlorotoluenes, eliminating option A.

Toluene yields xylene isomers upon methylation, while phenol produces cresols, eliminating options C and D.

Chlorobenzene undergoes methylation at ortho and para positions relative to the chlorine substituent,
yielding precisely 1-chloro-2-methylbenzene and 1-chloro-4-methylbenzene as specified.

$\mathrm{C_6H_5Cl} + \mathrm{CH_3Cl} \xrightarrow[\mathrm{AlCl_3}]{}\text{1-chloro-2-methylbenzene} + \text{1-chloro-4-methylbenzene}$

The correct identity of A is chlorobenzene.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The solubility product of salt $\mathrm{B}_2 \mathrm{~A}$ is $3.2 \times 10^{-11}$ at 298 K . What is solubility of the salt at same temperature ?
questions.solution:
The salt is $\mathrm{B}_2 \mathrm{A}$, which dissociates in water as $\mathrm{B}_2 \mathrm{A(s)} \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{B}^+\mathrm{(aq)} + \mathrm{A}^{2-}\mathrm{(aq)}$.

Let $s$ represent the molar solubility. From stoichiometry, $[\mathrm{B}^+] = 2s$ and $[\mathrm{A}^{2-}] = s$.

The solubility product is $K_{sp} = [\mathrm{B}^+]^2 [\mathrm{A}^{2-}] = (2s)^2(s) = 4s^3$.

Given $K_{sp} = 3.2 \times 10^{-11}$, solving yields $4s^3 = 3.2 \times 10^{-11}$
$s^3 = \frac{3.2 \times 10^{-11}}{4} = 8 \times 10^{-12}$
$s = (8 \times 10^{-12})^{1/3} = 2 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{mol\, dm}^{-3}$.

This value corresponds to option C.

The answer is $\boxed{\text{C}}$.

questions.q: What is pH of weak dibasic acid, that is $2 \%$ dissociated in its $\mathrm{M} / 100$ solution at 298 K ?
questions.solution:
To determine the pH of a weak dibasic acid solution at concentration $C = 0.01$ M with 2% dissociation, the following approach applies.

As each dibasic acid molecule $H_2A$ contributes two $H^+$ ions upon dissociation, the hydrogen ion concentration is $[H^+] = 2 \times C \times 0.02 = 2 \times 0.01 \times 0.02 = 0.0004$ M.

Thus, pH $= -\log_{10}(0.0004) = -\log_{10}(4 \times 10^{-4}) = -(\log_{10}4 + \log_{10}10^{-4})$. Since $\log_{10}4 \approx 0.6020$ and $\log_{10}10^{-4} = -4$, we have pH $= -(0.6020 - 4) = -(-3.3980) = 3.3980$.

This value closely matches option C.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following xenon compound has chlorine pentafluoride like structure?
questions.solution:
Xenon compounds share structural similarities with interhalogens when their molecular geometries match. Chlorine pentafluoride ($ClF_5$) has a square pyramidal geometry arising from an octahedral electron domain with one lone pair and five bonding pairs.

Among xenon compounds, XeF_4$ is square planar, XeF_6$ is distorted octahedral, and XeO_3$ is pyramidal. XeOF_4$ features xenon bonded to four fluorine atoms and one oxygen atom via a double bond, yielding five bonding domains and one lone pair. This $sp^3d^2$ hybridized configuration results in a square pyramidal geometry identical to $ClF_5$.

The xenon compound with structure analogous to $ClF_5$ is $\boxed{\text{D}}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is oxidation state of xenon in xenonmonooxytetrafluoride?
questions.solution:
The oxidation state of xenon in xenonmonooxytetrafluoride ($XeOF_4$) is determined by considering the known oxidation states of oxygen and fluorine. Oxygen typically has an oxidation state of $-2$, and fluorine is always $-1$ in compounds. Since $XeOF_4$ is neutral, the sum of the oxidation states is zero.

Let $x$ be the oxidation state of xenon. The equation becomes:

$x + (-2) + 4(-1) = 0$

Simplifying: $x - 2 - 4 = 0$

Thus, $x - 6 = 0$ and $x = +6$.

The oxidation state of xenon is +6, corresponding to answer choice C.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the monomers used in preparation of dacron .
questions.solution:
Dacron (Terylene) is a polyester formed by condensation polymerization between a dicarboxylic acid and a diol. The specific monomers are ethylene glycol (ethane-1,2-diol) and terephthalic acid (benzene-1,4-dicarboxylic acid).

Option A represents phenol and formaldehyde, monomers for Bakelite. Option B contains 1,3-butadiene and acrylonitrile, monomers for Buna-N rubber. Option D includes acrylonitrile and phenol, unrelated to polyester synthesis.

Option C contains the correct monomers: $\mathrm{HO}(\mathrm{CH}_2)_2\mathrm{OH}$ (ethylene glycol) and $\mathrm{HO}\mathrm{C}(=\mathrm{O})\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_4\mathrm{C}(=\mathrm{O})\mathrm{OH}$ (terephthalic acid).

The final answer is $\boxed{\text{C}}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following polymers is used to obtain surgical sutures?
questions.solution:
Surgical sutures require materials with high tensile strength, flexibility, and biocompatibility. Among common polymers, Nylon 6 (polyamide) possesses these properties and is widely employed as a non-absorbable suture material.

Terylene (polyethylene terephthalate) is primarily used in textiles and packaging, while neoprene (polychloroprene) serves industrial applications requiring chemical resistance. Though Nylon 6,6 shares some characteristics, Nylon 6 remains the standard choice due to its specific mechanical and biological performance.

The polymer used for surgical sutures is $\boxed{A}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the oxidation number of carbon in methanal?
questions.solution:
Oxidation number calculation for methanal (HCHO):

In a neutral molecule, the sum of oxidation numbers equals zero. Hydrogen has oxidation number $+1$ and oxygen $-2$ in this compound.

Let $x$ be the oxidation number of carbon. The sum is:

$x + 2(+1) + (-2) = 0$

Simplifying:

$x + 2 - 2 = 0$

$x = 0$

The oxidation number of carbon in methanal is $\boxed{0}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Calculate the number of unit cells in $1 \mathrm{~cm}^3$ of an element if unit cell edge length is $2.0 \times 10^{-8} \mathrm{~cm}$
questions.solution:
The volume of a cubic unit cell with edge length $a = 2.0 \times 10^{-8}\,\text{cm}$ is $V = a^3 = (2.0 \times 10^{-8})^3 = 8.0 \times 10^{-24}\,\text{cm}^3$.

For a total volume of $1\,\text{cm}^3$, the number of unit cells is $N = \frac{1}{8.0 \times 10^{-24}} = 0.125 \times 10^{24} = 1.25 \times 10^{23}$.

Matching with the given options, this corresponds to C.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Calculate the radius of an atom of an element in pm if it forms bcc unit cell structure having edge length $4.3 \times 10^{-8} \mathrm{~cm}$.
questions.solution:
Body-centered cubic structure atoms contact along the body diagonal, whose length equals $4r$.

The body diagonal relates to edge length $a$ through spatial geometry: $a\sqrt{3} = 4r$.

Isolating the radius yields $r = \frac{a\sqrt{3}}{4}$.

Given edge length $a = 4.3 \times 10^{-8}$ cm converts to $a = 430$ pm using $1$ cm $= 10^{10}$ pm.

Substitution gives $r = \frac{430 \times \sqrt{3}}{4}$.

With $\sqrt{3} \approx 1.732$, the calculation proceeds: $r = \frac{430 \times 1.732}{4} = \frac{744.76}{4} = 186.19$ pm.

The approximate radius of $186.2$ pm corresponds to option A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Calculate cryoscopic constant of solvent if depression in freezing point of 0.18 m solution of nonvolatile solute is 0.2 K
questions.solution:
The cryoscopic constant $K_f$ relates freezing point depression $\Delta T_f$ and molality $m$ through the colligative property equation $\Delta T_f = K_f \cdot m$.

Given $\Delta T_f = 0.2\text{ K}$ and $m = 0.18\text{ mol kg}^{-1}$, solving for $K_f$ yields:

$K_f = \frac{\Delta T_f}{m} = \frac{0.2}{0.18} = \frac{10}{9} \approx 1.11\text{ K kg mol}^{-1}$.

This value corresponds to option (C).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Which of the following aqueous solutions having same molality exhibits maximum boiling point elevation?
(Assume complete dissociation)
questions.solution:
Boiling point elevation is a colligative property given by the formula $\Delta T_b = i \cdot K_b \cdot m$, where $K_b$ and $m$ are constant for all aqueous solutions. The elevation is therefore proportional to the van't Hoff factor $i$.

For each solute:

KCl dissociates as $\mathrm{KCl} \to \mathrm{K}^+ + \mathrm{Cl}^-$, giving $i = 2$.

NaCl dissociates as $\mathrm{NaCl} \to \mathrm{Na}^+ + \mathrm{Cl}^-$, giving $i = 2$.

AlCl₃ dissociates as $\mathrm{AlCl_3} \to \mathrm{Al}^{3+} + 3\mathrm{Cl}^-$, giving $i = 4$.

BaCl₂ dissociates as $\mathrm{BaCl_2} \to \mathrm{Ba}^{2+} + 2\mathrm{Cl}^-$, giving $i = 3$.

The highest van't Hoff factor is $i = 4$ for AlCl₃, which therefore exhibits the maximum boiling point elevation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Calculate the mole fraction of pure liquid $B$ in solution if total vapour pressure of solution, vapour pressure of pure liquid A and vapour pressure of pure liquid B are $500 \mathrm{mmHg}, 400 \mathrm{~mm} \mathrm{Hg}$ and 575 mm Hg respectively at given temperature.
questions.solution:
To determine the mole fraction of liquid B, Raoult's law is applied to the ideal solution. The total vapor pressure is expressed as $P_{\text{total}} = (1 - X_B) P_A^0 + X_B P_B^0$, given $P_{\text{total}} = 500\,\text{mmHg}$, $P_A^0 = 400\,\text{mmHg}$, and $P_B^0 = 575\,\text{mmHg}$.

$500 = (1 - X_B) \cdot 400 + X_B \cdot 575$

Simplifying this equation results in $100 = 175 X_B$, yielding $X_B = \frac{100}{175} = \frac{4}{7} \approx 0.5714$.

This value corresponds to option B, confirming the mole fraction of B is $\boxed{\text{B}}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Calculate number of molecules present in 5.4 g of urea (Molar mass of urea $=60 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$ )
questions.solution:
The number of moles $n$ is determined from the given mass and molar mass: $n = \frac{5.4}{60} = 0.09 \text{ mol}$.

Multiplying by Avogadro's number yields the number of molecules: $0.09 \times 6.022 \times 10^{23} = 5.4198 \times 10^{22}$.

Comparing with the options, the value $5.419 \times 10^{22}$ corresponds to choice B.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
A container consists mixture of four gases as $5 \mathrm{~g~} \mathrm{H}_2, 8 \mathrm{~g~} \mathrm{He}, 50 \mathrm{~g~} \mathrm{CO}_2$ and 20 g Ne at a certain temperature. Which of the following gases exerts minimum partial pressure?
\(\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|} \hline \mathrm{X}=x & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 \\ \hline \mathrm{P}(\mathrm{X}=x) & 0.1 & 0.2 & 0.3 & 0.4 \\ \hline \end{array}\)
questions.solution:
Dalton's Law of Partial Pressures states that the partial pressure of each gas in a mixture is the product of its mole fraction and the total pressure: $P_i = X_i P_{\text{total}}$. Since $P_{\text{total}}$ is constant, the partial pressure is proportional to the mole fraction, which depends on the number of moles: $X_i = \frac{n_i}{n_{\text{total}}}$. Therefore, the gas with the fewest moles exerts the minimum partial pressure.

Moles are determined from mass and molar mass using $n = \frac{\text{mass}}{\text{molar mass}}$.
The molar masses are: $2$ g/mol for $\mathrm{H}_2$, $4$ g/mol for $\mathrm{He}$, $44$ g/mol for $\mathrm{CO}_2$, and $20$ g/mol for $\mathrm{Ne}$.

Calculating for each gas:
$n_{\mathrm{H}_2} = \frac{5}{2} = 2.5$ mol
$n_{\mathrm{He}} = \frac{8}{4} = 2.0$ mol
$n_{\mathrm{CO}_2} = \frac{50}{44} \approx 1.136$ mol
$n_{\mathrm{Ne}} = \frac{20}{20} = 1.0$ mol

The minimum number of moles is $1.0$ mol for neon, which will exert the minimum partial pressure.

$\boxed{\text{D}}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: "Pairing of electrons in the orbitals belonging to the same subshell does not occur unless each orbital belonging to that subshell has got one electron each." This statement is known as
questions.solution:
The statement "Pairing of electrons in the orbitals belonging to the same subshell does not occur unless each orbital belonging to that subshell has got one electron each" constitutes the definition of Hund's rule of maximum multiplicity.

This posited rule mandates that, within degenerate orbitals of a given subshell, each orbital is occupied by a single electron possessing parallel spin prior to any electron pairing occurring, thereby maximizing unpaired electrons and minimizing inter-electronic repulsion.

Among the alternatives, Pauli's exclusion principle ($|$n, l, m_l$, m_s$|$ must be unique per electron) concerns the maximum occupancy and quantum state uniqueness of an orbital; Aufbau's rule specifies the order of orbital filling by energy; and Heisenberg's uncertainty principle ($\Delta x \Delta p \geq \frac{\hbar}{2}$) pertains to fundamental measurement limitations. The statement refers exclusively to Hund's rule.

$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which instrument is used for determination of particle size?
questions.solution:
Particle size determination requires direct imaging capabilities provided by electron microscopy techniques. SEM offers surface visualization for measuring particle dimensions through high-resolution topography, while TEM achieves higher resolution for nanoscale internal structure analysis and particle measurement.

Spectroscopic methods prove unsuitable for direct size determination: FTIR identifies functional groups and chemical composition, and UV-visible spectroscopy quantifies concentrations and electronic transitions, though it may provide indirect size information through plasmon resonance effects in specific cases.

The instruments directly capable of particle size determination are $\boxed{\text{A, B}}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Calculate the work done if 1 mole of certain gas compressed isothermally and reversibly at 300 K from initial pressure $x$ bar to final pressure $2 x$ bar $\left[\mathrm{R}=8 \cdot 314 \mathrm{~J} \mathrm{~K}^{-1} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}\right]$
questions.solution:
Work during isothermal reversible compression of an ideal gas:

The work done is given by $\mathrm{W} = -\mathrm{nRT} \ln\left(\frac{\mathrm{P}_1}{\mathrm{P}_2}\right)$.

Substituting the given values: $n = 1\ \text{mol}$, $T = 300\ \text{K}$, $R = 8.314\ \text{J}\ \text{K}^{-1}\ \text{mol}^{-1}$, and $\frac{\mathrm{P}_1}{\mathrm{P}_2} = \frac{x}{2x} = \frac{1}{2}$.

$\mathrm{W} = -(1) \times (8.314) \times (300) \times \ln\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)$

$\mathrm{W} = -2494.2 \times \ln\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)$

Since $\ln\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = -\ln(2) \approx -0.6931$:

$\mathrm{W} = -2494.2 \times (-0.6931) = 1728.86\ \text{J}$

Converting to kilojoules: $\mathrm{W} = 1.72886\ \text{kJ} \approx 1.729\ \text{kJ}$

The positive value indicates work is done on the system during compression, and this matches option A.

$\boxed{A}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Calculate the standard enthalpy change of following reaction.
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{CH}_{4(\mathrm{~g})}+2 \mathrm{O}_{2(\mathrm{~g})} \rightarrow \mathrm{CO}_{2(\mathrm{~g})}+2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}_{(\ell)} \\
& \text { if } \quad \Delta_{\mathrm{f}} \mathrm{H}^{\circ}\left(C H_4\right)=-75 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1} \\
& \Delta_{\mathrm{f}} \mathrm{H}^{\circ}\left(C \mathrm{O}_2\right)=-390 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1} \\
& \Delta_{\mathrm{f}} \mathrm{H}^{\circ}\left(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\right)=-286 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}
\end{aligned}$
questions.solution:
The standard enthalpy change of the reaction is calculated using the formula:

$\Delta_{\mathrm{r}} \mathrm{H}^{\circ} = \sum n \Delta_{\mathrm{f}} \mathrm{H}^{\circ}(\text{products}) - \sum m \Delta_{\mathrm{f}} \mathrm{H}^{\circ}(\text{reactants})$

For the reaction $\mathrm{CH}_{4(\mathrm{g})} + 2\mathrm{O}_{2(\mathrm{g})} \rightarrow \mathrm{CO}_{2(\mathrm{g})} + 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_{(\ell)}$ with given enthalpies: $\Delta_{\mathrm{f}} \mathrm{H}^{\circ}(\mathrm{CH}_4) = -75\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$, $\Delta_{\mathrm{f}} \mathrm{H}^{\circ}(\mathrm{CO}_2) = -390\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$, $\Delta_{\mathrm{f}} \mathrm{H}^{\circ}(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}) = -286\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$, and noting $\Delta_{\mathrm{f}} \mathrm{H}^{\circ}(\mathrm{O}_2) = 0\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$:

$\Delta_{\mathrm{r}} \mathrm{H}^{\circ} = [1 \times (-390) + 2 \times (-286)] - [1 \times (-75) + 2 \times 0] = [-390 - 572] - [-75] = -962 + 75 = -887\ \mathrm{kJ}$

The standard enthalpy change of the reaction is $-887\ \mathrm{kJ}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify from following the correct set of thermodynamic conditions for the reaction to be spontaneous at all temperature.
questions.solution:
The spontaneity of a reaction is determined by the sign of the Gibbs free energy change, given by $\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S$, where $\Delta G \lt 0$ indicates a spontaneous process.

For a reaction to be spontaneous at all temperatures, both terms must contribute negatively to $\Delta G$. When $\Delta H \lt 0$ and $\Delta S \gt 0$, the equation becomes $\Delta G = (\text{negative}) - T(\text{positive})$. Since $-T\Delta S$ is always negative under these conditions, $\Delta G$ remains negative regardless of temperature.

In contrast, other combinations show temperature dependence or constant non-spontaneity:
$\Delta H \gt 0$, $\Delta S \gt 0$: spontaneous only at high temperatures
$\Delta H \lt 0$, $\Delta S \lt 0$: spontaneous only at low temperatures
$\Delta H \gt 0$, $\Delta S \lt 0$: non-spontaneous at all temperatures

The condition satisfying spontaneity at all temperatures corresponds to $\Delta H \lt 0$ and $\Delta S \gt 0$.

Answer: $\boxed{C}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $x$ and y are sides of two squares such that $\mathrm{y}=x-x^2$, then the rate of change of area of the second square with respect to that of the first square is
questions.solution:
Let $x$ represent the side length of the first square and $y$ the side length of the second. The area of the first square is $A_1 = x^2$, and the area of the second is $A_2 = y^2$.

Given that $y = x - x^2$, we express $A_2$ in terms of $x$ as $A_2 = (x - x^2)^2 = x^2(1 - x)^2 = x^2(1 - 2x + x^2) = x^4 - 2x^3 + x^2$.

The rate of change $\frac{dA_2}{dA_1}$ is found using the chain rule: $\frac{dA_2}{dA_1} = \frac{dA_2/dx}{dA_1/dx}$.

Differentiating $A_1 = x^2$ gives $\frac{dA_1}{dx} = 2x$.
Differentiating $A_2 = x^4 - 2x^3 + x^2$ yields $\frac{dA_2}{dx} = 4x^3 - 6x^2 + 2x$.

Substituting these into the chain rule expression:

$\frac{dA_2}{dA_1} = \frac{4x^3 - 6x^2 + 2x}{2x}$.

For $x \gt 0$, factor and simplify:

$\frac{dA_2}{dA_1} = \frac{2x(2x^2 - 3x + 1)}{2x} = 2x^2 - 3x + 1$.

This result corresponds to option C.

The final answer is $\boxed{\text{C}}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The function $\mathrm{f}(x)=[x(x-2)]^2$ is increasing in the set
questions.solution:
To determine where $f(x)=[x(x-2)]^2$ is increasing, we analyze the sign of its derivative. Rewriting gives $f(x)=(x^2-2x)^2$.

Differentiating yields $f'(x)=2(x^2-2x)(2x-2)=4x(x-1)(x-2)$.

The critical points are $x=0$, $x=1$, and $x=2$.

Evaluating the sign of $f'(x)$ in the intervals:

On $(-\infty,0)$, $f'(x)\lt 0$ (decreasing).

On $(0,1)$, $f'(x) \gt 0$ (increasing).

On $(1,2)$, $f'(x)\lt 0$ (decreasing).

On $(2,\infty)$, $f'(x) \gt 0$ (increasing).

The function is increasing on $(0,1) \cup (2,\infty)$, corresponding to option D.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The minimum value of $\mathrm{a} x+$ by where $x \mathrm{y}=\mathrm{c}^2$ is
questions.solution:
Given $E = ax + by$ with constraint $xy = c^2$. Expressing $y = \frac{c^2}{x}$, we obtain $E(x) = ax + \frac{bc^2}{x}$.

Differentiating yields $E'(x) = a - \frac{bc^2}{x^2}$. Setting $E'(x) = 0$ gives $x^2 = \frac{bc^2}{a}$, so $x = \pm c\sqrt{\frac{b}{a}}$.

For $x = c\sqrt{\frac{b}{a}}$, $y = c\sqrt{\frac{a}{b}}$, and $E = 2c\sqrt{ab}$. For $x = -c\sqrt{\frac{b}{a}}$, $y = -c\sqrt{\frac{a}{b}}$, and $E = -2c\sqrt{ab}$.

The second derivative $E''(x) = \frac{2bc^2}{x^3}$ shows the first gives a local minimum and the second a local maximum. Since $E(x) \to -\infty$ as $x \to 0^-$ or $x \to -\infty$, no global minimum exists, but the minimal local extremum is $-2c\sqrt{ab}$.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{C}}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The equation of the tangent to the curve $y=b e^{-x / a}$ at the point where it crosses the Y axis is
questions.solution:
The curve $y = b e^{-x/a}$ crosses the Y-axis at $x=0$, giving the point of tangency $(0, b)$.

The derivative is computed as $\frac{dy}{dx} = -\frac{b}{a} e^{-x/a}$.

At $x=0$, the slope of the tangent is $\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)_{x=0} = -\frac{b}{a}$.

Using point-slope form with point $(0, b)$ yields $y - b = -\frac{b}{a} x$.

Multiplying through by $a$ gives $a(y - b) = -b x$, rearranged to $b x + a y = a b$.

Dividing both sides by $a b$ results in $\frac{x}{a} + \frac{y}{b} = 1$, which corresponds to option B.

The final answer is $\boxed{\text{B}}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the area bounded by the curve $x^2=4 \mathrm{y}$, X-axis and the line $x=4$ is divided into equal areas by the line $x=\alpha$, then the value of $\alpha$ is ...
questions.solution:
The area under the curve $x^2 = 4y$ from $x = 0$ to $x = 4$ is found by integrating $y = \frac{x^2}{4}$ over this interval.

$A_{\text{total}} = \int_{0}^{4} \frac{x^2}{4} dx = \frac{1}{4} \left[ \frac{x^3}{3} \right]_{0}^{4} = \frac{1}{4} \cdot \frac{64}{3} = \frac{16}{3}$

The line $x = \alpha$ divides this region into two equal areas, so the area from $x = 0$ to $x = \alpha$ must be $\frac{8}{3}$.

$\int_{0}^{\alpha} \frac{x^2}{4} dx = \frac{8}{3} \implies \frac{1}{4} \left[ \frac{x^3}{3} \right]_{0}^{\alpha} = \frac{8}{3} \implies \frac{\alpha^3}{12} = \frac{8}{3}$

Solving gives $\alpha^3 = 32 \implies \alpha = 32^{1/3}$, which corresponds to option D.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $p^3=q^4=r^6=t^7=s^2$, then $\log _t(p q r s)=\ldots$.
questions.solution:
Let $p^3 = q^4 = r^6 = t^7 = s^2 = k$. Then $p = k^{1/3}$, $q = k^{1/4}$, $r = k^{1/6}$, $t = k^{1/7}$, and $s = k^{1/2}$.

The product $pqrs = k^{1/3} \cdot k^{1/4} \cdot k^{1/6} \cdot k^{1/2} = k^{(1/3) + (1/4) + (1/6) + (1/2)}$. Converting to a common denominator of 12 yields $\frac{4}{12} + \frac{3}{12} + \frac{2}{12} + \frac{6}{12} = \frac{15}{12} = \frac{5}{4}$, so $pqrs = k^{5/4}$.

Evaluating $\log_t(pqrs)$ gives $\log_{k^{1/7}}(k^{5/4}) = \frac{5/4}{1/7} \log_k k = \frac{5}{4} \cdot 7 = \frac{35}{4}$.

Final answer: $\frac{35}{4}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two tangents to the circle $x^2+y^2=4$ at the points $A$ and $B$ meet at $\mathrm{P}(-4,0)$. Then the area of quadrilateral PAOB , where 'O' is the origin is
questions.solution:
The circle $x^2 + y^2 = 4$ has center $O(0,0)$ and radius $2$ units.
The external point is $P(-4,0)$ with $OP = 4$ units.

Tangents from $P$ touch the circle at $A$ and $B$, forming right angles with radii $OA$ and $OB$.
The quadrilateral $PAOB$ consists of two congruent right triangles.

Using the Pythagorean theorem in $\triangle OAP$:
$PA^2 = OP^2 - OA^2 = 16 - 4 = 12$, so $PA = 2\sqrt{3}$ units.

The area of $\triangle OAP$ is $\frac{1}{2} \cdot OA \cdot PA = \frac{1}{2} \cdot 2 \cdot 2\sqrt{3} = 2\sqrt{3}$ sq. units.

Area of quadrilateral $PAOB = 2 \times 2\sqrt{3} = 4\sqrt{3}$ sq. units.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let z be the complex number such that $|\mathrm{z}|+\mathrm{z}=3+\mathrm{i}$ where $i=\sqrt{-1}$, then $|\mathrm{z}|=$
questions.solution:
Let $z = x + iy$ where $x, y \in \mathbb{R}$ with modulus $|z| = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}$. Given the equation $|z| + z = 3 + i$, substitute to obtain:

$\sqrt{x^2 + y^2} + x + iy = 3 + i$

Equating real and imaginary parts yields $y = 1$ and $\sqrt{x^2 + 1} + x = 3$.

Solving the real equation: $\sqrt{x^2 + 1} = 3 - x$. Squaring both sides gives $x^2 + 1 = 9 - 6x + x^2$, which simplifies to $6x = 8$, so $x = \frac{4}{3}$.

Thus $z = \frac{4}{3} + i$ and $|z| = \sqrt{(\frac{4}{3})^2 + 1^2} = \sqrt{\frac{16}{9} + \frac{9}{9}} = \sqrt{\frac{25}{9}} = \frac{5}{3}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let $\mathrm{f}(x)= \begin{cases}\frac{x^4-5 x^2+4}{|(x-1)(x-2)|} & , x \neq 1,2 \\ 6 & , x=1 \\ 12 & , x=2\end{cases}$ then $\mathrm{f}(x)$ is continuous on the set
questions.solution:
Continuity analysis for $f(x)= egin{cases} rac{x^4-5 x^2+4}{|(x-1)(x-2)|} & , x eq 1,2 \ 6 & , x=1 \ 12 & , x=2\end{cases}$

The expression simplifies to $ rac{(x-1)(x+1)(x-2)(x+2)}{|x-1||x-2|}$ for $x eq 1,2$.

At $x=1$, the left-hand limit evaluates to $(1+1)(1+2) = 6$, while the right-hand limit gives $-(1+1)(1+2) = -6$. The limit does not exist, so $f$ is discontinuous at $x=1$.

At $x=2$, the left-hand limit yields $-(2+1)(2+2) = -12$, and the right-hand limit gives $(2+1)(2+2) = 12$. The limit does not exist, confirming discontinuity at $x=2$.

For $x eq 1,2$, $f$ is continuous as it consists of rational functions with non-zero denominators.

The function is continuous on $\mathbb{R} - \{1,2\}$, confirming answer $ oxed{ ext{D}}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\int_0^1 x\left|x-\frac{1}{2}\right| \mathrm{d} x=$
questions.solution:
The integrand $x\left|x-\frac{1}{2}\right|$ has a discontinuity in its derivative at $x = \frac{1}{2}$, requiring integration over two intervals.

For $x \lt \frac{1}{2}$, $\left|x-\frac{1}{2}\right| = \frac{1}{2} - x$. For $x \geq \frac{1}{2}$, $\left|x-\frac{1}{2}\right| = x - \frac{1}{2}$. The integral splits accordingly:

$\int_0^1 x\left|x-\frac{1}{2}\right| dx = \int_0^{1/2} x\left(\frac{1}{2} - x\right) dx + \int_{1/2}^1 x\left(x - \frac{1}{2}\right) dx$

The first integral evaluates as:

$\int_0^{1/2} \left(\frac{x}{2} - x^2\right) dx = \left[\frac{x^2}{4} - \frac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^{1/2} = \frac{1}{16} - \frac{1}{24} = \frac{1}{48}$

The second integral yields:

$\int_{1/2}^1 \left(x^2 - \frac{x}{2}\right) dx = \left[\frac{x^3}{3} - \frac{x^2}{4}\right]_{1/2}^1 = \left(\frac{1}{3} - \frac{1}{4}\right) - \left(\frac{1}{24} - \frac{1}{16}\right) = \frac{1}{12} + \frac{1}{48} = \frac{5}{48}$

Summing both parts gives $\frac{1}{48} + \frac{5}{48} = \frac{6}{48} = \frac{1}{8}$.

Final result: $\boxed{\frac{1}{8}}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \frac{300 \sin x+100 \cos x}{\sin x+\cos x} \mathrm{~d} x=\ldots$
questions.solution:
Evaluate the integral: $I = \int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \frac{300 \sin x+100 \cos x}{\sin x+\cos x} \, \mathrm{d} x$

Apply the transformation $x \mapsto \frac{\pi}{2} - x$, using the identity $\int_a^b f(x) \, \mathrm{d} x = \int_a^b f(a+b-x) \, \mathrm{d} x$:

$I = \int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \frac{300 \cos x+100 \sin x}{\cos x+\sin x} \, \mathrm{d} x$

Add this to the original integral:

$2I = \int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \frac{400 \sin x+400 \cos x}{\sin x+\cos x} \, \mathrm{d} x = 400 \int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \, \mathrm{d} x$

Evaluate the integral:

$2I = 400 \cdot \frac{\pi}{2} = 200\pi$

Result: $I = 100\pi$

This corresponds to option A.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The equation of the curve passing through the point $(0,2)$ given that the sum of the ordinate and abscissa of any point exceeds the slope of the tangent to the curve at that point by 5 is
questions.solution:
The curve $y = f(x)$ satisfies that for any point $(x, y)$, the sum of the abscissa and ordinate exceeds the slope of the tangent by 5: $y + x = \frac{dy}{dx} + 5$. Rearranging gives the linear differential equation $\frac{dy}{dx} - y = x - 5$.

With $P(x) = -1$ and $Q(x) = x - 5$, the integrating factor is $e^{-x}$. The general solution is $y \cdot e^{-x} = \int (x - 5)e^{-x} \, dx + C$.

Using integration by parts, $\int (x - 5)e^{-x} \, dx = e^{-x}(4 - x)$, yielding $y \cdot e^{-x} = e^{-x}(4 - x) + C$. Dividing by $e^{-x}$ gives $y = 4 - x + Ce^x$.

Applying the initial condition $y(0) = 2$ leads to $2 = 4 + C$, so $C = -2$.

Substituting gives $y = 4 - x - 2e^x$, corresponding to option B.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The solution of the differential equation. $(1+x) \frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{d} x}-x \mathrm{y}=1-x$ is
options: $\mathrm{y}(1+x)=x+\mathrm{ce}^x$, where c is the constant of integration
$\mathrm{y}(1+x)=\mathrm{ce}^x$, where c is the constant of integration
$\mathrm{y}(1-x)=x-\mathrm{ce}^x$, where c is the constant of integration
$\mathrm{y}(1+x)=x~ \mathrm{ce}^{-x}$, where c is the constant of integration
questions.solution:
Convert the differential equation to standard form by dividing through by $1+x$:

$\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} - \frac{x}{1+x}y = \frac{1-x}{1+x}$

Identify $P(x) = -\frac{x}{1+x}$ and compute the integrating factor:

$\int P(x)\,\mathrm{d}x = \int \left(-1 + \frac{1}{1+x}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x = -x + \ln|1+x|$

$\text{IF} = e^{-x + \ln|1+x|} = (1+x)e^{-x}$

Multiply through by the integrating factor and integrate:

$y(1+x)e^{-x} = \int (1-x)e^{-x}\,\mathrm{d}x + C$

Evaluate the integral using integration by parts with $u = 1-x$, $\mathrm{d}v = e^{-x}\,\mathrm{d}x$:

$\int (1-x)e^{-x}\,\mathrm{d}x = (1-x)(-e^{-x}) - \int (-e^{-x})(-\mathrm{d}x) = -(1-x)e^{-x} - e^{-x} = xe^{-x}$

Substitute back and solve for $y$:

$y(1+x)e^{-x} = xe^{-x} + C$

$y(1+x) = x + Ce^x$

This matches option A.

questions.q: The differential equation representing the family of parabolas having vertex at the origin and axis along the positive Y-axis is
questions.solution:
Family of parabolas with vertex at origin and axis along positive Y-axis: $x^2 = 4ay$ where $a$ is an arbitrary constant.

Differentiating both sides with respect to $x$ yields:

$2x = 4a \frac{dy}{dx}$

Eliminate $a$ by substituting $4a = \frac{x^2}{y}$ (for $y \neq 0$):

$2x = \left(\frac{x^2}{y}\right) \frac{dy}{dx}$

Multiplying both sides by $y$ and dividing by $x$ (for $x \neq 0$):

$2y = x \frac{dy}{dx}$

Rewriting gives the differential equation:

$x \frac{dy}{dx} - 2y = 0$

This corresponds to option A.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The population of towns $A$ and $B$ increase at the rate proportional to their population present at that time. At the end of the year 1984, the population of both the towns was 20,000 . At the end of the year 1989, the population of town A was 25,000 and that of town B was 28,000. The difference of populations of towns A and B at the end of 1994 was
questions.solution:
The population growth of both towns follows the exponential model $P(t) = P_0 e^{kt}$, with initial population $P_0 = 20,\!000$ at $t=0$ (end of 1984).

For town A, the population at $t=5$ (end of 1989) is $25,\!000$, giving $e^{5k_A} = 25,\!000 / 20,\!000 = 1.25$.
The population at $t=10$ (end of 1994) is therefore $P_A(10) = 20,\!000 (1.25)^2 = 31,\!250$.

For town B, the population at $t=5$ is $28,\!000$, yielding $e^{5k_B} = 28,\!000 / 20,\!000 = 1.4$.
The population at $t=10$ is $P_B(10) = 20,\!000 (1.4)^2 = 39,\!200$.

The difference in populations at the end of 1994 is $39,\!200 - 31,\!250 = \boxed{7950}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\mathrm{u}=\log (\sqrt{x-1}-\sqrt{x+1})$ and $\mathrm{v}=\sqrt{x+1}+\sqrt{x-1}$ then $\frac{\mathrm{du}}{\mathrm{dv}}=\ldots$.
questions.solution:
The function v is given by $v = \sqrt{x+1} + \sqrt{x-1}$, with the condition that $x \geq 1$ for real-valued square roots. Its product with the conjugate expression gives:

$v(\sqrt{x+1} - \sqrt{x-1}) = (\sqrt{x+1})^2 - (\sqrt{x-1})^2 = (x+1) - (x-1) = 2$

Solving for the conjugate, $\sqrt{x+1} - \sqrt{x-1} = \frac{2}{v}$.

The original expression for u, $u = \log(\sqrt{x-1} - \sqrt{x+1})$, simplifies as:

$\sqrt{x-1} - \sqrt{x+1} = -(\sqrt{x+1} - \sqrt{x-1}) = -\frac{2}{v}$

Assuming real-valued functions, the logarithm of a negative number is undefined. Given that this is a derivative problem, we proceed with the absolute value or consider the form $u = \log(\frac{2}{v})$ for $v \gt 0$, yielding:

$u = \log 2 - \log v$

Differentiating with respect to $v$:

$\frac{du}{dv} = -\frac{1}{v}$

This corresponds to option D, which remains consistent even under complex analysis considerations.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{D}}$

questions.q: If $\mathrm{f}(x)=3 x^2+2 x \mathrm{f}^{\prime}(1)+\mathrm{f}^{\prime \prime}(2)$, then $\mathrm{f}(x)=$ ______
questions.solution:
Given the function $\mathrm{f}(x)=3x^2+2x\mathrm{f}^{\prime}(1)+\mathrm{f}^{\prime\prime}(2)$, the derivative terms are constants since they are evaluated at specific points.
Define $A = \mathrm{f}^{\prime}(1)$ and $B = \mathrm{f}^{\prime\prime}(2)$, thus $\mathrm{f}(x) = 3x^2 + 2A x + B$.

Differentiating yields $\mathrm{f}^{\prime}(x) = 6x + 2A$ and further, $\mathrm{f}^{\prime\prime}(x) = 6$.

From $\mathrm{f}^{\prime\prime}(x) = 6$, it follows that $B = 6$.

Substituting $x=1$ into $\mathrm{f}^{\prime}(x)$ gives $A = 6(1) + 2A$, leading to $A = -6$.

The function becomes $\mathrm{f}(x) = 3x^2 - 12x + 6$, which corresponds to option C.

$\boxed{\text{C}}$

questions.q: The tangent to the ellipse $9 x^2+16 y^2=288$ making equal intercepts on the co-ordinate axes intersects the X -axis and the Y -axis in the points $A$ and $B$ respectively. Then $A(\triangle O A B)=$ (where O is origin)
questions.solution:
A line tangent to the ellipse $\frac{x^2}{32} + \frac{y^2}{18} = 1$ and making equal intercepts on the coordinate axes has equation $x + y = k$, where $k$ is the intercept length.

The condition for tangency $c^2 = a^2m^2 + b^2$ gives $k^2 = (32)(-1)^2 + 18 = 50$.

The triangle $\triangle OAB$ is formed by the line with intercept $k$ intersecting the axes at $A(k, 0)$ and $B(0, k)$, and the origin $O(0, 0)$.

The area is given by $\frac{1}{2} |k| \cdot |k| = \frac{1}{2}k^2 = \frac{1}{2} \cdot 50 = 25$ square units.

questions.q: $\int \frac{\mathrm{d} x}{\sin ^2 x \cos ^2 x}=$
options: $\tan x+\cot x+\mathrm{c}$, where c is the constant of integration.
$\tan x-\cot x+\mathrm{c}$, where c is the constant of integration.
$\tan x \cot x+\mathrm{c}, \quad$ where c is the constant of integration.
$\tan x-\cot 2 x+c$, where $c$ is the constant of integration.
questions.solution:
The integral $\int \frac{\mathrm{d} x}{\sin^2 x \cos^2 x}$ can be evaluated using trigonometric identities. Starting from $\frac{1}{\sin^2 x \cos^2 x} = \frac{\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x}{\sin^2 x \cos^2 x}$, this simplifies to $\frac{1}{\cos^2 x} + \frac{1}{\sin^2 x} = \sec^2 x + \csc^2 x$.

Integrating term by term gives $\int \sec^2 x \, \mathrm{d} x + \int \csc^2 x \, \mathrm{d} x = \tan x - \cot x + C$.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{B}}$

questions.q:
$\int \frac{d x}{x^{\frac{1}{2}}+x^{\frac{1}{3}}}=\mathrm{A} x^{\frac{1}{2}}+\mathrm{B} x^{\frac{1}{3}}+\mathrm{C} x^{\frac{1}{6}}+\mathrm{D} \log \left(x^{\frac{1}{6}}+1\right)+\mathrm{k}$
(where k is the integration constant) then values of $A, B, C$ and $D$ are respectively,
questions.solution:
To evaluate $\int \frac{dx}{x^{\frac{1}{2}} + x^{\frac{1}{3}}}$, substitute $x = t^6$, which yields $dx = 6t^5dt$, $x^{\frac{1}{2}} = t^3$, and $x^{\frac{1}{3}} = t^2$.

Substituting gives $\int \frac{6t^5dt}{t^3 + t^2} = \int \frac{6t^3dt}{t+1}$.

Dividing $t^3$ by $t+1$ produces $t^2 - t + 1 - \frac{1}{t+1}$, so the integral becomes $6\int(t^2 - t + 1 - \frac{1}{t+1})dt$.

Integrating term by term yields $6(\frac{t^3}{3} - \frac{t^2}{2} + t - \log|t+1|) = 2t^3 - 3t^2 + 6t - 6\log|t+1|$.

Substituting $t = x^{\frac{1}{6}}$ gives $2x^{\frac{1}{2}} - 3x^{\frac{1}{3}} + 6x^{\frac{1}{6}} - 6\log(x^{\frac{1}{6}}+1)$ + k, using the fact that $x^{\frac{1}{6}}+1 \gt 0$ for $x \gt 0$.

Matching to the form $Ax^{\frac{1}{2}}+Bx^{\frac{1}{3}}+Cx^{\frac{1}{6}}+D\log(x^{\frac{1}{6}}+1)$ + k gives A = 2, B = -3, C = 6, and D = -6.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\int x^2 \cos x \mathrm{~d} x=$
options: $x^2 \sin x+2 x \cos x-2 \sin x+\mathrm{c}$ where c is the constant of integration
$x^2 \sin x-2 x \cos x-2 \sin x+\mathrm{c}$ where $c$ is the constant of integration

$x^2 \sin x-2 x \cos x+2 \sin x+c$
where c is the constant of integration

$x^2 \sin x+2 x \cos x+2 \sin x+c$
where $c$ is the constant of integration
questions.solution:
To evaluate $\int x^2 \cos x \, dx$, apply integration by parts twice. Let $u = x^2$ and $dv = \cos x \, dx$, so $du = 2x \, dx$ and $v = \sin x$. Then,

$\int x^2 \cos x \, dx = x^2 \sin x - 2 \int x \sin x \, dx$.

For the remaining integral, let $u = x$ and $dv = \sin x \, dx$, giving $du = dx$ and $v = -\cos x$. Thus,

$\int x \sin x \, dx = -x \cos x + \int \cos x \, dx = -x \cos x + \sin x$.

Substituting back,

$\int x^2 \cos x \, dx = x^2 \sin x - 2(-x \cos x + \sin x) + c = x^2 \sin x + 2x \cos x - 2 \sin x + c$,

where $c$ is the constant of integration. The result corresponds to option A.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\cot ^{-1}(\sqrt{\cos \alpha})-\tan ^{-1}(\sqrt{\cos \alpha})=x$, then the value of $\sin x$ is
questions.solution:
Given the expression $x = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{\tan(\frac{\theta}{2})}\right) - \tan^{-1}\left(\tan(\frac{\theta}{2})\right)$.

Using the identity $\tan^{-1}(y) + \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{y}\right) = \frac{\pi}{2}$ for $y \gt 0$
where $y = \tan(\frac{\theta}{2})$, we have:
$\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{\tan(\frac{\theta}{2})}\right) = \frac{\pi}{2} - \tan^{-1}\left(\tan(\frac{\theta}{2})\right)$

Substituting into the expression for $x$:
$x = \left(\frac{\pi}{2} - \tan^{-1}\left(\tan(\frac{\theta}{2})\right)\right) - \tan^{-1}\left(\tan(\frac{\theta}{2})\right)$
$x = \frac{\pi}{2} - 2\tan^{-1}\left(\tan(\frac{\theta}{2})\right)$

Considering the given alternative form $\cot^{-1}(\sqrt{\cos\alpha}) - \tan^{-1}(\sqrt{\cos\alpha}) = x$
Using $\cot^{-1} y = \frac{\pi}{2} - \tan^{-1} y$:
$x = \left(\frac{\pi}{2} - \tan^{-1}(\sqrt{\cos\alpha})\right) - \tan^{-1}(\sqrt{\cos\alpha})$
$x = \frac{\pi}{2} - 2\tan^{-1}(\sqrt{\cos\alpha})$

To find $\sin x$:
$\sin x = \sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - 2\tan^{-1}(\sqrt{\cos\alpha})\right)$
Using $\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - \theta\right) = \cos\theta$:
$\sin x = \cos\left(2\tan^{-1}(\sqrt{\cos\alpha})\right)$

Let $y = \sqrt{\cos\alpha}$ and $\theta = \tan^{-1}(y)$, so $\tan\theta = y$
Using the identity $\cos(2\theta) = \frac{1 - \tan^2\theta}{1 + \tan^2\theta}$:
$\sin x = \frac{1 - y^2}{1 + y^2} = \frac{1 - \cos\alpha}{1 + \cos\alpha}$

Applying half-angle identities:
$\sin x = \frac{2\sin^2(\frac{\alpha}{2})}{2\cos^2(\frac{\alpha}{2})} = \frac{\sin^2(\frac{\alpha}{2})}{\cos^2(\frac{\alpha}{2})} = \tan^2\left(\frac{\alpha}{2}\right)$

The final answer is $\boxed{\text{D}}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Considering only the principal values of the inverse trigonometric functions, the value of $\tan \left(\sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{3}{5}\right)-2 \cos ^{-1}\left(\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\right)\right)$ is
questions.solution:
Let $E = \tan\left(\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{3}{5}\right) - 2\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\right)\right)$.

Evaluate the inverse trigonometric expressions: Let $\alpha = \sin^{-1}\left(\frac{3}{5}\right)$, so $\sin\alpha = \frac{3}{5}$ and $\tan\alpha = \frac{3}{4}$. Let $\beta = \cos^{-1}\left(\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\right)$, so $\cos\beta = \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}$ and $\tan\beta = \frac{1}{2}$.

Compute the double angle: Using $\tan(2\beta) = \frac{2\tan\beta}{1 - \tan^2\beta}$, we obtain $\tan(2\beta) = \frac{2\cdot\frac{1}{2}}{1 - \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2} = \frac{4}{3}$.

Apply the tangent subtraction formula: $E = \tan(\alpha - 2\beta) = \frac{\tan\alpha - \tan(2\beta)}{1 + \tan\alpha\tan(2\beta)} = \frac{\frac{3}{4} - \frac{4}{3}}{1 + \frac{3}{4}\cdot\frac{4}{3}} = \frac{-\frac{7}{12}}{2} = -\frac{7}{24}$.

Final result: $\boxed{-\frac{7}{24}}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $y=\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{1+x+x^2}\right)+\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{x^2+3 x+3}\right)+\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{x^2+5 x+7}\right)$ then the value of $\mathrm{y}^{\prime}(0)$ is
questions.solution:
Given: $y = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{1+x+x^2}\right) + \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{x^2+3x+3}\right) + \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{x^2+5x+7}\right)$

Each term simplifies using the identity $\tan^{-1}(A) - \tan^{-1}(B) = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{A-B}{1+AB}\right)$:

$\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{1+x+x^2}\right) = \tan^{-1}(x+1) - \tan^{-1}(x)$

$\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{x^2+3x+3}\right) = \tan^{-1}(x+2) - \tan^{-1}(x+1)$

$\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{x^2+5x+7}\right) = \tan^{-1}(x+3) - \tan^{-1}(x+2)$

Substituting simplifies $y$ to a telescoping sum:
$y = \tan^{-1}(x+3) - \tan^{-1}(x)$

Differentiate:
$y'(x) = \frac{1}{1+(x+3)^2} - \frac{1}{1+x^2}$

Evaluate at $x = 0$:
$y'(0) = \frac{1}{10} - 1 = -\frac{9}{10}$

Result: $y'(0) = -\frac{9}{10}$

The correct choice is $\boxed{\text{C}}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{\mathrm{e}^{x^2}-\cos 3 x}{\sin x \log (1+2 x)}=$
questions.solution:
The limit

$\lim_{x \to 0} \frac{e^{x^2} - \cos 3x}{\sin x \log (1 + 2x)}$

is of the indeterminate form $\frac{0}{0}$ as $x \to 0$.

Use standard approximations near zero: $e^u - 1 \approx u$, $1 - \cos u \approx \frac{u^2}{2}$, $\sin u \approx u$, and $\log(1 + u) \approx u$.

Rewrite the numerator as $(e^{x^2} - 1) - (\cos 3x - 1) = (e^{x^2} - 1) + (1 - \cos 3x) \approx x^2 + \frac{(3x)^2}{2} = x^2 + \frac{9x^2}{2} = \frac{11x^2}{2}$.
The denominator approximates to $(x)(2x) = 2x^2$.

Substitute into the limit:

$\lim_{x \to 0} \frac{\frac{11x^2}{2}}{2x^2} = \frac{11}{4}$

The limit evaluates to $\boxed{\frac{11}{4}}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A manufacturing company produces two items, A and B. Each toy should be processed by two machines, I and II. Machine I can be operated for maximum 10 hours 40 minutes. It takes 20 minutes for an item A and 15 minutes for B. Machine II can be operated for a total time at 8 hours 20 minutes. It takes 5 minutes for an item $A$ and 8 minutes for $B$. The profit per item of $A$ is $₹ 25$ and per item of $B$ is ₹18. The formulation of an L.P.P. to maximize the profit (where $x$ is number of items $A$ and $y$ is the number of item $B$ ) is _____
options: $\begin{array}{r}\text { Maximize } \mathrm{z}=25 x+18 \mathrm{y} \\ \text { subject to } 20 x+15 y \leqslant 640 \\ \qquad 5 x+8 y \leqslant 500 \\ \qquad x, y \geqslant 0\end{array}$
$\begin{aligned} & \text { Maximize } \mathrm{z}=25 x+18 \mathrm{y} \\ & \text { subject to } 20 x+5 y \leqslant 8 \\ & \qquad 5 x+8 y \leqslant 10 \\ & x, y \geqslant 0\end{aligned}$

$\begin{array}{r}\text { Maximize } \mathrm{z}=25 x+18 \mathrm{y} \\ \text { subject to } 4 x+3 y \leqslant 128 \\ \qquad \begin{array}{r}5 x+8 y \geqslant 500 \\ x, y \geqslant 0\end{array}\end{array}$
questions.solution:
The linear programming problem requires maximizing profit given machine time constraints. Let $x$ and $y$ represent the quantities produced of items A and B respectively.

The objective function to maximize is $Z = 25x + 18y$, representing the total profit.

Machine I operates for 640 minutes (10 hours 40 minutes), with processing times of 20 minutes per unit of A and 15 minutes per unit of B, yielding the constraint $20x + 15y \leqslant 640$.

Machine II operates for 500 minutes (8 hours 20 minutes), with processing times of 5 minutes per unit of A and 8 minutes per unit of B, giving $5x + 8y \leqslant 500$.

Non-negativity constraints require $x \geqslant 0$ and $y \geqslant 0$.

The complete formulation matches Option B:
Maximize $Z = 25x + 18y$
Subject to:
$20x + 15y \leqslant 640$
$5x + 8y \leqslant 500$
$x, y \geqslant 0$

questions.q:
If p, q, r, s are statements, where, $p: A^2-B^2=(A-B)(A+B) ; A, B$ are matrices, $A B \neq B A$
q: $5 \leqslant 5$
r: ${ }^8 \mathrm{C}_1+{ }^8 \mathrm{C}_2+{ }^8 \mathrm{C}_3+\ldots \ldots \ldots . .+{ }^8 \mathrm{C}_8=256$
s: Maximum value of ${ }^8 \mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{r}}$ is 70 then the statement from the following having truth value true is ....
questions.solution:
Statement p: $A^2-B^2=(A-B)(A+B)$ with matrices $A,B$ where $AB eq BA$.

Expanding the right side gives $(A-B)(A+B) = A^2 + AB - BA - B^2$. For $A^2-B^2$ to equal this expression, $AB$ must equal $BA$, but by hypothesis $AB eq BA$. Thus, $p$ is false.

Statement q: $5 \leqslant 5$ is true since equality holds.

Statement r: ${}^8C_1 + {}^8C_2 + \ldots + {}^8C_8$.

The full sum from $k=0$ to $8$ is $2^8 = 256$, so the given sum is $256 - {}^8C_0 = 255$. Since $255 eq 256$, $r$ is false.

Statement s: Maximum value of ${}^8C_r$ occurs at $r=4$ and equals $ rac{8!}{4!4!} = 70$, so $s$ is true.

Evaluating options:

Option A: $(p \wedge \sim r) \vee (\sim q \wedge \sim s) = (F \wedge T) \vee (F \wedge F) = F \vee F = F$

Option B: $(p \vee \sim q) \leftrightarrow (\sim r ightarrow s) = (F \vee F) \leftrightarrow (T ightarrow T) = F \leftrightarrow T = F$

Option C: $(p \leftrightarrow q) \wedge (\sim p \vee \sim q) = (F \leftrightarrow T) \wedge (T \vee F) = F \wedge T = F$

Option D: $(s \vee \sim p) \leftrightarrow (\sim p \wedge \sim r) = (T \vee T) \leftrightarrow (T \wedge T) = T \leftrightarrow T = T$

The only true statement is Option D.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $A$ is a matrix of order 2 and $I$ is the identity matrix of order 2 such that $\mathrm{A}^2-4 \mathrm{~A}+3 \mathrm{I}=0$ then $(\mathrm{A}+3 \mathrm{I})^{-1}=$
questions.solution:
Given the matrix equation $A^2 - 4A + 3I = 0$, we seek the inverse of $A + 3I$.

Let $X = A + 3I$, so that $A = X - 3I$. Substituting into the given equation:

$(X - 3I)^2 - 4(X - 3I) + 3I = 0$

Expanding, since $X$ and $I$ commute:

$X^2 - 6X + 9I - 4X + 12I + 3I = 0$

Combining terms:

$X^2 - 10X + 24I = 0$

Rewriting to isolate $24I$:

$24I = 10X - X^2$

Factoring the right side:

$24I = X(10I - X)$

Multiplying both sides on the right by $X^{-1}$:

$24X^{-1} = 10I - X$

Solving for $X^{-1}$:

$X^{-1} = \frac{1}{24}(10I - X)$

Substituting $X = A + 3I$:

$(A + 3I)^{-1} = \frac{1}{24}(7I - A)$

This matches option C.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the pair of lines $3 x^2-5 x y+p y^2=0$ and $6 x^2-x y-5 y^2=0$ have one line common, then $\mathrm{p}=$
questions.solution:
Let the two pairs of lines be given by:

$3x^2 - 5xy + py^2 = 0$

$6x^2 - xy - 5y^2 = 0$

Assume the common line has slope $m$, so its equation is $y = mx$.
Substitute into the second pair's equation and divide by $x^2$:

$6 - m - 5m^2 = 0 \Rightarrow 5m^2 + m - 6 = 0$

Factorizing: $(m - 1)(5m + 6) = 0 \Rightarrow m = 1 \text{ or } m = -\frac{6}{5}$

Substitute each slope into the first pair's equation $3 - 5m + pm^2 = 0$:

For $m = 1$: $3 - 5(1) + p(1)^2 = 0 \Rightarrow p = 2$

For $m = -\frac{6}{5}$: $3 - 5\left(-\frac{6}{5}\right) + p\left(\frac{36}{25}\right) = 0 \Rightarrow 9 + \frac{36p}{25} = 0 \Rightarrow p = -\frac{25}{4}$

Thus, $p$ can be either $2$ or $-\frac{25}{4}$.

Matching with the options, the answer is $\boxed{\text{C}}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The number of ways in which 6 boys and 4 girls can be seated around a round table such that 2 special boys and a special girl never sit together is
questions.solution:
Circular arrangements with restrictions are computed using complementary counting. The total arrangements of 10 distinct people around a circular table is $(10-1)! = 9!$.

To count arrangements where two special boys and one special girl always sit together, treat them as a single block. Within this block, they can be arranged in $3!$ ways. With the block considered as one entity, there remain 7 people, giving $(8-1)! = 7!$ circular arrangements. The number of restricted arrangements is therefore $3! \times 7!$.

The number of valid arrangements where the specified individuals never sit together is:

$9! - (3! \times 7!) = 362880 - 30240 = 332640$

The final answer is $\boxed{332640}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The probability that a non leap year selected at random will contain 52 Saturdays or 53 Sundays is
questions.solution:
A non-leap year consists of 365 days, which equals 52 weeks and 1 odd day.

The odd day can be any day of the week with equal probability, so the sample space has 7 equally likely outcomes.

Let A be the event of having exactly 52 Saturdays. This occurs when the odd day is not Saturday, giving 6 favorable outcomes: Monday through Friday and Sunday.

Let B be the event of having 53 Sundays. This requires the odd day to be Sunday, with exactly 1 favorable outcome.

The probability of A or B occurring is given by $P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A \cap B)$.

The intersection $A \cap B$ occurs when the odd day is Sunday, since this gives both 52 Saturdays and 53 Sundays. Thus $P(A \cap B) = P(B) = \frac{1}{7}$.

Substituting the probabilities: $P(A \cup B) = \frac{6}{7} + \frac{1}{7} - \frac{1}{7} = \frac{6}{7}$.

$\boxed{\frac{6}{7}}$

questions.q:
A random variable X has the following probability distribution :
\(\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|} \hline \mathrm{X}=x & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 \\ \hline \mathrm{P}(\mathrm{X}=x) & 0 \cdot 1 & 0 \cdot 2 & 0 \cdot 3 & 0 \cdot 4 \\ \hline \end{array}\)
The mean and standard deviation of X are respectively
questions.solution:
The mean $E(X)$ and standard deviation $\sigma$ are calculated from the given probability distribution using standard formulas.

$E(X) = \sum x_i P(X=x_i) = (1)(0.1) + (2)(0.2) + (3)(0.3) + (4)(0.4) = 3.0$

$E(X^2) = \sum x_i^2 P(X=x_i) = (1)(0.1) + (4)(0.2) + (9)(0.3) + (16)(0.4) = 10.0$

The variance is $\text{Var}(X) = E(X^2) - [E(X)]^2 = 10.0 - 9.0 = 1.0$,
giving standard deviation $\sigma = \sqrt{1.0} = 1$.

The values $E(X)=3$ and $\sigma=1$ correspond to option B.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{B}}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A fair n faced die is rolled repeatedly until a number less than n appears. If the mean of the number of tosses required is $\frac{\mathrm{n}}{9}$, then $\mathrm{n}=$ (where $\mathrm{n} \in \mathbb{N}$ )
questions.solution:
The die has $n$ faces with outcomes $\{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$. A success occurs when rolling a number less than $n$, of which there are $n - 1$ favorable outcomes. The probability of success in a single toss is $p = \frac{n-1}{n}$.

Let $X$ denote the number of tosses until a success. Since $X$ follows a geometric distribution, its expected value is $E[X] = \frac{1}{p} = \frac{n}{n-1}$.

Given that $E[X] = \frac{n}{9}$, we set $\frac{n}{n-1} = \frac{n}{9}$. For $n \geq 2$, dividing both sides by $n$ yields $\frac{1}{n-1} = \frac{1}{9}$, so $n - 1 = 9$ and $n = 10$.

The value of $n$ is 10, corresponding to answer choice D.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A fair coin is tossed a fixed number of times. If the probability of getting 5 tails is same as the probability of getting 7 tails, then the probability of getting 3 tails is
questions.solution:
Given equal probabilities for exactly 5 and 7 tails in $n$ coin tosses, we establish $\binom{n}{5} = \binom{n}{7}$ after eliminating the common $\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^n$ factor.

Using the symmetry property $\binom{n}{k} = \binom{n}{n-k}$, the equality implies $5 + 7 = n$, yielding $n = 12$.

The probability of exactly 3 tails is $\binom{12}{3} \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{12}$. Calculating $\binom{12}{3} = 220$, we obtain $P(X=3) = \frac{220}{2^{12}} = \frac{55}{2^{10}}$.

This matches option B.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: In a triangle ABC with usual notations if $\angle A=30^{\circ}$, then the value of $\left(1+\frac{a}{c}+\frac{b}{c}\right)\left(1+\frac{c}{b}-\frac{a}{b}\right)=$
questions.solution:
Given expression: $E = \left(1+\frac{a}{c}+\frac{b}{c}\right)\left(1+\frac{c}{b}-\frac{a}{b}\right)$

Combine terms over common denominators:

$E = \left(\frac{c+a+b}{c}\right)\left(\frac{b+c-a}{b}\right) = \frac{(a+b+c)(b+c-a)}{bc}$

Recognize the numerator as a difference of squares where $X = b+c$ and $Y = a$:

$E = \frac{(b+c)^{2} - a^{2}}{bc}$

Expanding gives:

$E = \frac{b^{2} + c^{2} + 2bc - a^{2}}{bc}$

Using the Law of Cosines, $a^{2} = b^{2} + c^{2} - 2bc \cos A$, so $b^{2} + c^{2} - a^{2} = 2bc \cos A$. Substituting:

$E = \frac{2bc \cos A + 2bc}{bc} = 2(\cos A + 1)$

Given $A = 30^{\circ}$ and $\cos 30^{\circ} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$, then:

$E = 2\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} + 1\right) = \sqrt{3} + 2$

This matches option C.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{C}}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: In a triangle $P Q R$ with usual notations, $\angle R=\frac{\pi}{2}$. If $\tan \frac{p}{2}$ and $\tan \frac{q}{2}$ are the roots of the equation. $a x^2+b x+c=0 \quad(a \neq 0)$, then
questions.solution:
Given that $\angle R = \frac{\pi}{2}$ in triangle $PQR$, the angle sum property implies $P + Q = \frac{\pi}{2}$, so $\frac{P}{2} + \frac{Q}{2} = \frac{\pi}{4}$.

Taking tangent on both sides and applying the identity for $\tan\left(\frac{P}{2} + \frac{Q}{2}\right)$ yields:

$\frac{\tan\left(\frac{P}{2}\right) + \tan\left(\frac{Q}{2}\right)}{1 - \tan\left(\frac{P}{2}\right)\tan\left(\frac{Q}{2}\right)} = 1$

Since $\tan\left(\frac{P}{2}\right)$ and $\tan\left(\frac{Q}{2}\right)$ are roots of $ax^2 + bx + c = 0$, by Vieta’s formulas their sum is $-\frac{b}{a}$ and product is $\frac{c}{a}$.

Substituting into the trigonometric equation gives:

$\frac{-\frac{b}{a}}{1 - \frac{c}{a}} = 1$

Simplifying leads to $-b = a - c$, or equivalently $a + b = c$.

Final answer: $\boxed{A}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the angles $A, B$ and $C$ of a triangle are in A.P. and if $a, b$ and $c$ denote the length of the sides opposite to $A, B$ and $C$ respectively, then the value of $\frac{a}{b} \sin 2 B+\frac{b}{a} \sin 2 A$ is
questions.solution:
Given that angles $A$, $B$, and $C$ of a triangle are in arithmetic progression, and $A + B + C = 180^\circ$.

Since $A$, $B$, $C$ form an AP, $2B = A + C$.
Substituting yields $2B + B = 180^\circ$, so $3B = 180^\circ$ and $B = 60^\circ$.

Evaluate $E = \frac{a}{b} \sin 2B + \frac{b}{a} \sin 2A$.
By the Sine Rule, $\frac{a}{\sin A} = \frac{b}{\sin B}$, so $\frac{a}{b} = \frac{\sin A}{\sin B}$ and $\frac{b}{a} = \frac{\sin B}{\sin A}$.

Thus $E = \left(\frac{\sin A}{\sin B}\right) \sin 2B + \left(\frac{\sin B}{\sin A}\right) \sin 2A$.
Apply $\sin 2x = 2 \sin x \cos x$:
$E = \left(\frac{\sin A}{\sin B}\right)(2 \sin B \cos B) + \left(\frac{\sin B}{\sin A}\right)(2 \sin A \cos A)$.
Simplify to $E = 2 \sin A \cos B + 2 \sin B \cos A = 2(\sin A \cos B + \cos A \sin B)$.

Recognize the sine sum identity: $E = 2 \sin(A + B) = 2 \sin(180^\circ - C) = 2 \sin C$.

Since $B = 60^\circ$ and angles are in AP, $A = 60^\circ - d$, $C = 60^\circ + d$ for some $d$, but the provided options imply a constant result. For the equilateral case ($d = 0$), $C = 60^\circ$.
Then $E = 2 \sin 60^\circ = 2 \cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = \sqrt{3}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The acute angle between the line $4 x-2 y+13=0$ and the line which makes equal intercepts with the co-ordinate axes is
questions.solution:
To determine the acute angle between the lines, begin by finding their slopes. The first line, $4x - 2y + 13 = 0$, can be rearranged to slope-intercept form: $2y = 4x + 13$, yielding $y = 2x + \frac{13}{2}$, so $m_1 = 2$.

The second line makes equal intercepts on the axes. For intercept $a$, its equation is $x + y = a$, or in slope-intercept form, $y = -x + a$, so $m_2 = -1$.

The acute angle $\theta$ between lines with slopes $m_1$ and $m_2$ is given by $\tan \theta = \left| \frac{m_1 - m_2}{1 + m_1 m_2} \right|$. Substituting $m_1 = 2$ and $m_2 = -1$, compute $\tan \theta = \left| \frac{2 + 1}{1 - 2} \right| = \left| \frac{3}{-1} \right| = 3$.
Thus, $\theta = \tan^{-1}(3)$.

The final answer is $\boxed{\text{B}}$.

questions.q: The lines $\frac{6 x-6}{18}=\frac{y+1}{3}=\frac{z-1}{5}$ and $\frac{3 x+6}{12}=\frac{y-1}{3}=\frac{z+1}{2}$ are $\ldots$
questions.solution:

The first line simplifies to $\frac{x-1}{3} = \frac{y+1}{3} = \frac{z-1}{5}$, passing through $P_1(1, -1, 1)$ with direction vector $\vec{d_1} = (3, 3, 5)$.

The second line simplifies to $\frac{x+2}{4} = \frac{y-1}{3} = \frac{z+1}{2}$, passing through $P_2(-2, 1, -1)$ with direction vector $\vec{d_2} = (4, 3, 2)$.

Parallelism Check: Since $\frac{3}{4} \neq \frac{3}{3} \neq \frac{5}{2}$, the direction vectors are not proportional; the lines are not parallel.

Intersection Check: Parameterize Line 1 as $x = 3\lambda + 1$, $y = 3\lambda - 1$, $z = 5\lambda + 1$ and Line 2 as $x = 4\mu - 2$, $y = 3\mu + 1$, $z = 2\mu - 1$.
Equating $x$ and $y$ gives $3\lambda - 4\mu = -3$ and $3\lambda - 3\mu = 2$, solving to $\mu = 5$ and $\lambda = 17/3$.
Substituting into $z$ yields $55/3 = -2$, a contradiction.

As the lines are not parallel and do not intersect, they are skew.

Thus, the relationship is skew lines, and the correct option is C.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The line $\frac{x-1}{2}=\frac{y+2}{-1}=\frac{\mathrm{z}}{1}$ intersects the XY plane and the YZ plane at points $A$ and $B$ respectively. The equation of line through the points $A$ and $B$ is
questions.solution:
Find the line through A and B, where A is the intersection of the line $\frac{x-1}{2}=\frac{y+2}{-1}=\frac{z}{1}$ with the XY plane ($z=0$), and B is its intersection with the YZ plane ($x=0$).

Set $z=0$ and $\frac{z}{1}=0$ in the parametric ratio, yielding $\frac{x-1}{2}=0$ and $\frac{y+2}{-1}=0$. Thus, $x=1$, $y=-2$, and $A$ is $(1, -2, 0)$.

Set $x=0$ and denote $\frac{0-1}{2} = -\frac{1}{2}$. From $\frac{y+2}{-1} = -\frac{1}{2}$, cross-multiplying gives $y+2 = \frac{1}{2}$, so $y = -\frac{3}{2}$. Similarly, $\frac{z}{1} = -\frac{1}{2}$, so $z = -\frac{1}{2}$, and $B$ is $\left(0, -\frac{3}{2}, -\frac{1}{2}\right)$.

The direction vector from A to B is $\vec{b} - \vec{a} = (0-1)\hat{i} + \left(-\frac{3}{2} + 2\right)\hat{j} + \left(-\frac{1}{2} - 0\right)\hat{k} = -\hat{i} + \frac{1}{2}\hat{j} - \frac{1}{2}\hat{k}$.

Using point A and this direction, the vector equation is $\left[\vec{r} - (\hat{i} - 2\hat{j})\right] \times \left(-\hat{i} + \frac{1}{2}\hat{j} - \frac{1}{2}\hat{k}\right) = \overline{0}$, matching option A.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The distance of the point $A(3,-4,5)$ from the plane $2 x+5 y-6 z=16$ measured along the line $\frac{x}{2}=\frac{y}{1}=\frac{z}{-2}$ is
questions.solution:
The distance from $A(3,-4,5)$ to the plane $2x+5y-6z=16$ measured along the direction $(2,1,-2)$ is determined by finding the intersection point of the line through $A$ parallel to this direction with the plane.

The parametric equations of the line are $x=3+2\lambda$, $y=-4+\lambda$, $z=5-2\lambda$. Substituting into the plane equation yields:

$2(3+2\lambda)+5(-4+\lambda)-6(5-2\lambda)=16$

$21\lambda-44=16$

$\lambda=\frac{60}{21}=\frac{20}{7}$

The intersection point coordinates are:

$x_B=3+2\cdot\frac{20}{7}=\frac{61}{7}$

$y_B=-4+\frac{20}{7}=\frac{-8}{7}$

$z_B=5-2\cdot\frac{20}{7}=\frac{-5}{7}$

The distance $AB$ is calculated as:

$\sqrt{\left(\frac{61}{7}-3\right)^2+\left(\frac{-8}{7}+4\right)^2+\left(\frac{-5}{7}-5\right)^2}$

$\sqrt{\left(\frac{40}{7}\right)^2+\left(\frac{20}{7}\right)^2+\left(\frac{-40}{7}\right)^2}$

$\sqrt{\frac{1600+400+1600}{49}}=\sqrt{\frac{3600}{49}}=\frac{60}{7}$

The distance measured along the given line is $\frac{60}{7}$ units.

questions.q: The direction cosines of a normal to the plane passing throgh $(4,2,3)$, $(-1,4,2)$ and $(3,2,1)$ are .....
questions.solution:
Given points $A(4,2,3)$, $B(-1,4,2)$, and $C(3,2,1)$, vectors in the plane are identified as $\vec{AB} = (-5,2,-1)$ and $\vec{AC} = (-1,0,-2)$.

Direction cosines are obtained by dividing each component by the magnitude $|\vec{n}| = \sqrt{101}$, yielding $\left(\frac{-4}{\sqrt{101}}, \frac{-9}{\sqrt{101}}, \frac{2}{\sqrt{101}}\right)$, which corresponds to option C.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The unit vectors perpendicular to the plane determined by the points $\mathrm{A}(1,-1,2) \mathrm{~B}(2,0,-1) \mathrm{~C}(0,2,1)$ is
questions.solution:
Perpendicular unit vectors to the plane determined by points $A(1,-1,2)$, $B(2,0,-1)$, and $C(0,2,1)$ can be found by computing the cross product of two vectors in the plane.

The vectors $\vec{AB} = (2-1)\hat{i} + (0-(-1))\hat{j} + (-1-2)\hat{k} = \hat{i} + \hat{j} - 3\hat{k}$ and $\vec{AC} = (0-1)\hat{i} + (2-(-1))\hat{j} + (1-2)\hat{k} = -\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - \hat{k}$ lie in the plane.

The cross product $\vec{N} = \vec{AB} \times \vec{AC}$ yields a vector perpendicular to the plane:

$\vec{N} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 1 & 1 & -3 \\ -1 & 3 & -1 \end{vmatrix} = \hat{i}(1 \cdot (-1) - (-3) \cdot 3) - \hat{j}(1 \cdot (-1) - (-3) \cdot (-1)) + \hat{k}(1 \cdot 3 - 1 \cdot (-1))$

$\vec{N} = \hat{i}(-1 + 9) - \hat{j}(-1 - 3) + \hat{k}(3 + 1) = 8\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}$

The magnitude is $|\vec{N}| = \sqrt{8^2 + 4^2 + 4^2} = \sqrt{96} = 4\sqrt{6}$.

The unit vectors are $\pm \frac{\vec{N}}{|\vec{N}|} = \pm \frac{8\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}}{4\sqrt{6}} = \pm \frac{4(2\hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k})}{4\sqrt{6}} = \pm \frac{2\hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}}{\sqrt{6}}$.

This corresponds to option C.

questions.q: The equation of the plane passing through the point $(1,1,1)$ and through the line of intersection of $x+2 y-z+1=0$ and $3 x-y-4 z+3=0$ is
questions.solution:
Plane through intersection and point

For planes $P_1: x+2y-z+1=0$ and $P_2: 3x-y-4z+3=0$, the family of planes through their line of intersection is given by $P_1 + \lambda P_2 = 0$:

$(x+2y-z+1) + \lambda(3x-y-4z+3) = 0$

Substituting point $(1,1,1)$ determines $\lambda$:

$3 + \lambda(1) = 0 \Rightarrow \lambda = -3$

$x+2y-z+1 - 3(3x-y-4z+3) = 0$

$-8x + 5y + 11z - 8 = 0$

Multiplying by $-1$ yields $8x - 5y - 11z + 8 = 0$, which corresponds to option C.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{C}}$
